summary.text: Male infant born at 36 weeks 5 days (2500 g, spontaneous vaginal delivery) was admitted on day 4 of life with jaundice, decreased feeding, fever and decreased urine output.

Workup showed unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia of 19.9 mg/dl, low total and ionized calcium, a normal chest X-ray, vitamin D insufficiency with normal iPTH, ALP and phosphorus, normal CSF analysis, sterile CSF and blood cultures and a normal cranial ultrasound.

He received intensive phototherapy and intravenous 10% calcium gluconate, then oral calcium with a further 48 hours of intravenous calcium; fever and respiratory distress subsided and he came off oxygen. He was discharged after 15 days of admission per the case text (the discussion states a 14-day stay) with sterile-culture neonatal sepsis, suspected meningitis, hyperbilirubinemia with ABO setting, hypocalcemia and vitamin D insufficiency.

At discharge he had erythematous swelling at a right-hand cannula site treated as thrombophlebitis; at one week follow up he had tender bony-hard swellings at previous cannulation sites without fluctuation or pus, and X-rays showed soft tissue calcification without bone extension, ruling out osteomyelitis.

Biopsy and ultrasound were declined by the parents. He was managed conservatively with oral paracetamol and avoidance of massage, and the lesions disappeared completely after 12 weeks without radiological confirmation.
